summary: Instagram is doing the heavy lifting: almost every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views, with a few exceptions. The best videos use a surprising 'it doesn't actually see/hear/think' hook about a simple robot or sensor (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR, line follower). Generic 'How does X work? 🤔' everyday-object titles (lift, tap, mall door, smoke detector, TV remote) get far less reach and almost no saves or shares.
winningPattern: Hindi, short 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' myth-busting hook about a hobby-robotics or Arduino-style sensor (gyro, clap switch, PIR, line follower, IR obstacle). Title states a counterintuitive claim in Hinglish with an emoji and #shorts, and is built around a robot or maker project rather than a household appliance. Posted on Instagram first, since it reliably gives 1,000+ views; YouTube only picked up the same style a few times (gyro, clap switch, PIR got 500-680 views). Clap switch topic worked twice, and a fresh angle on a proven topic is a safe bet.
doMore: Lead with a counterintuitive claim: 'X nahi karta, sirf Y karta hai' or 'Bina X ke ye Y ho jaata'.
Focus on robots and maker modules (gyro, IR, line follower, clap switch, PIR) that students can build themselves.
Make follow-up angles on proven hits, like the clap switch whistle video and other sensors tested in the same robot.
Add a save/share trigger at the end, such as 'Save karo project ke liye' or 'Dost ko bhejo jo robot banata hai'.
Keep posting daily in Hindi on Instagram, and copy the exact hook wording that worked on YouTube for the gyro, clap and PIR titles.
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects (lift, mall door, taps, smoke detector, TV remote), which average under 300 IG views.
Making several near-duplicate videos on one topic, like the 2 smoke detector, 2 tap and 2 IR sensor videos, which split the audience and lower each result.
Posting English videos with no Instagram version, since the one English video got only 161 YouTube views and nothing elsewhere.
